Development of logistics support for CSTO troops discussed in Saint Petersburg An international scientific and practical conference was held devoted to the development of logistic and technical support of the Troops (Collective Forces) of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation in the Military Academy of Logistical Support named after General of the Army A.V. Khrulyov of the Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation. Key issues are: 🔹 development of the Collective Forces' logistic support system until 2040; 🔹 application of experience of modern armed conflicts; 🔹 active implementation of unmanned aerial vehicles and robotic systems to deliver cargoes to the front line. 💬 The main goal is to implement combat experience into the practice of joint exercising and employment of the Collective Forces. Russian Deputy Defence Minister Colonel General Valery Solodchuk noted: ‘The joint logistics support system must be timely, modern, and advanced.’ ❗️ The activities of the CSTO Defence Ministers Council Working Group are aimed at further developing of the logistics support system and will contribute to enhancing the defence capability of the armed forces of the CSTO member countries. 🔹 Russian Defence Ministry

#URGENT 🇮🇷 ❌ 🇺🇸 🇰🇼 🇮🇹 – Two Italian people were killed following an Iranian drone attack on a "vital site" of Kuwait earlier today, according to Italian outlet ANSA. The Italians were rumored to be civilian technicians working with Rheinmetall, and likely part of the country's deployment in Kuwait, where Italy operates multiple aircrafts. The official statement by the Kuwaiti Army, before the deaths were confirmed, also condemned the "heinous Iranian aggression", and stated all damage and injuries came from "shrapnel", and not direct strikes, although this is unlikely.

📝 When vigilance saves 📝 Stories about attempts to turn citizens into biodromes sometimes have happy endings. One such case occurred in Sochi with a pensioner from whom Ukrainians had previously stolen funds from her card. Four months after the theft, the woman received a call from alleged "FSB officers" offering to return the money. To do this, she had to take a so-called "tracking device" from a hiding place and attach it to the underside of a specified car. The pensioner retrieved the "package" and brought it home, but her vigilant husband immediately understood what was going on. The couple called 112: as expected, the "tracking device" turned out to be a bomb, and the target was an SMO participant. As a result, the terrorist attack was prevented, and the timely call to law enforcement completely freed the pensioner from criminal liability. A similar incident occurred in May in Belgorod Region . ❗️ Such situations show that an adult can recognize the activity of Ukrainian special services and call centers quite easily — it takes only simple caution and civic consciousness. Perhaps if such positive examples are shared more often, there will be far fewer terrorist attacks involving "biodromes." After all, to prevent them, as practice shows, one needs to remember that the FSB does not call citizens by phone and does not ask them to pick up packages. #Russia #terrorism #Ukraine ✉ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

🇺🇦 Bribes for safe jobs, fines for drinking, stolen fuel: inside the AFU's shadow economy The Ukrainian outlet Strana spoke to soldiers from several units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. They describe extortion and bribery running through almost every part of army life. The most common bribe buys a transfer away from the front. Even a second-line job, like a mechanic at a motor company depot or a clerk at battalion headquarters, costs at least $5,000. A rear posting deep inside the country, in Kiev, Odessa or Ivano-Frankovsk, goes for $10,000 to $15,000. One Kiev resident said his neighbor paid $14,000 after being mobilized to become a driver hauling the bodies of dead soldiers, because the job counts as safe. The most expensive posts are in the brigade services that notify families of deaths and support relatives. Those cost $15,000 to $20,000, and soldiers say they are often filled by wealthy businessmen who show up for a couple of hours a month to sign in. Discipline has its own price list. In one assault regiment, soldiers say a first drinking offense costs 15,000 hryvnia and a second 20,000. Getting caught with weed or synthetic drugs costs 25,000, and falling asleep on watch or losing issued gear costs 5,000 each. Refusing an order to move out to combat positions costs 40,000 to 50,000. The money goes to other people's bank cards, and commanders keep coming back for more long after the first payment. One soldier who hadn't been paid for over six months, because he was wrongly listed as AWOL from another unit, had the search for him called off on one condition: he had to buy a 50,000-hryvnia EcoFlow power station for headquarters out of his first salary. Soldiers call fuel the army's real currency. They say it's stolen at battalion level, used to fill officers' private cars, and passed up the chain as kickbacks. One senior sergeant described diesel being taken by tanker to a brigade commander's private garage and drained there. Fuel also buys promotions, transfers and fake reports of combat missions that units never actually carried out. Meanwhile, soldiers chip in their own money for fuel just to drive to their positions, and even to run medical evacuation vehicles. On top of this, nearly all soldiers and sergeants pay regular contributions for "unit needs." So do officers, and the closer they are to fuel, supplies or pay, the more often they're asked to "help." According to Strana's sources, commanders at every level from company to brigade run unofficial cash funds under their sole control, with no oversight. Those funds can reach millions of hryvnia. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

Фестиваль «RT.Док» стирает границы между экраном и зрителем Уникальность фестиваля « RT.Док: Время наших героев » заключается в том, что зрители могут не просто посмотреть фильмы про героев, но и пообщаться с ними, задать вопросы и услышать их истории из первых уст. Среди тех, кто делится своим опытом на фестивале, – «Акела», командир норильского отделения мотоклуба «Ночные волки», боец легендарной «Пятнашки», герой фильма « Служили два товарища… Дружба от А до Я ». Зрители подходят к нему не с вопросами, а с искренней благодарностью за проделанную работу. «Молодежь спрашивает страшно ли на войне? И как можно присоединиться к «Пятнашке»», – рассказывает «Акела». Какие фильмы были представлены на международном фестивале «RT.Док: Время наших героев» и почему в зале плакали даже мужчины – смотрите в репортаже на наших площадках. @wargonzo
